rationale: Both parse the board into rows of tokens and run a graph search over the six hex neighbours, so they are very close. A keeps get_winner trivially readable and puts the edge definitions inside _connects with comments ('X connects left to right'). It has a docstring, marks cells as seen when it enqueues them (so each cell is queued once), and skips blank lines when parsing. B passes the start and goal edges in as arguments, which is a reasonable generalisation, but it makes get_winner bulkier. B also recomputes the board dimensions in the helper, has no docstring or comments, and can push the same cell onto its stack several times before deduplicating it on pop. A's ordering of the cols computation before the empty-board check is a trivial nit. Overall A is marginally clearer.
